We expect that convergence will be fast when the parameters λ and γ are small and the system evolves to a disordered (gaseous) state, but the connectivity constraint makes proving this challenging. In contrast, we expect convergence to equilibrium will be slow in the ordered (solid) state when λ is large, but we conjecture that desirable compressed and aligned states will be reached quickly, long before the system is very close to stationarity.

Moreover, in both the Potts and clock model settings, in any configuration with sufficiently low-perimeter, one of the q orientations will dominate with high probability. Recall that N represents the number of sites of the lattice G∆ . To ensure that the proof of ergodicity from [7] carries over to our setting, we use a sufficiently large value of N , namely N ≥ (n + 1)2 , although we expect the results to hold for smaller N . ▶ Definition 2 (Compression). A simply connected configuration σ of n particles on a lattice is said to be α-compressed if its perimeter is at most α · pmin (n), where pmin (n) is the minimum possible perimeter of a configuration of n particles.
